title: Finite Galois descent for sections of an etale sheaf
statement: Let $L$ be a field, let $E/L$ be a finite Galois extension (finite and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], normal, with $Q=\operatorname{Aut}_L(E)$ [def-pc-field-extension]), and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on the small etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. The group $Q$ acts on $F(\operatorname{Spec}E)$ by pullback along the automorphisms of $\operatorname{Spec}E$ over $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Pullback along $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ identifies $F(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ bijectively with the subset of $Q$-invariant elements of $F(\operatorname{Spec}E)$.

source.place: Tag 04JM, Lemma lemma-global-sections-point, finite Galois descent argument

proof.text: The finite separable extension is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]. Its spectrum map is a singleton cover because both field spectra have one point. The sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], via Mathlib Presieve.isSheafFor_singleton and isSeparatedFor_singleton, supplies unique descent of compatible sections and injectivity.

Functoriality of pullback and the fact that every L-algebra automorphism fixes the structure map show that pullback of every downstairs section is invariant. The maps are the affine spectrum maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum], composed by etaleSpecMap_comp.

Use the section bijection and projection formulas of [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition]. For an invariant section s these formulas show beta(p1* s)=beta(p2* s), hence p1* s=p2* s by injectivity of beta. Any pair of maps from an etale object Z to Spec E over Spec L factors through the scheme self-pullback, and so the two restrictions of s to Z coincide. Apply singleton-cover unique gluing to descend s. Combine invariance, injectivity and descent into Set.BijOn.
